verdict: The cryptographic core survives the revision: per-recipient ElGamal with the AND-composed Schnorr/Chaum-Pedersen proof, exact torsion rejection, the strong-Fiat-Shamir transcript now bound to (group_uid, dek_commit, prev, epoch), verify_strict plus body||sig hashing, the record-hash DEK cache, S5 on every wrap-carrying record, and the carry-as-verified-subset rule (R4) compose soundly, and the version, accessor and AAD claims in 3.1/3.2/3.4 match the lockfile, iroh-base 1.0.3 and ed25519-dalek 3 (to_scalar() is clamped-and-reduced; as_signing_key() exists). The prior crypto findings are fixed except two seams the fixes themselves opened: (1) the new A5 rule refuses every backup-key replacement recovery, because the record's pinned set no longer contains the author (head.backup) while G4 forces that recovery to be a rotate; (2) the r_i hedge adopted verbatim from the prior review includes the sorted index, so the stuck-RNG cross-group M reuse the bunker-wide c0 set was introduced to catch is detected only when the backup/authority key happens to sort at the same index in both groups, and the bunker-wide seen-commit set is inert because commits are group-salted. Beyond those, S9/S10 as written refuse the authority's own revocation carry (breaking the 'always wins' guarantee D13 was built for), S5 is not told to skip staged rows whose source no longer matches (a delete+recreate between export and snapshot stalls every client rotation), the server-authored rotate has no policy for an undecryptable retained row (the group stays write-fenced with the kicked key's wrap opening live M, forever), and neither the client pin file nor group_pin holds enough to verify the first record after a pinned head (A2/R2/R4/R6/C4 need the head record's content, not its hash). All are local rule or wording fixes; the record layout and the proof do not change.

unfixed_prior.prior_title: [MAJOR] crypto-A: R5's per-group 'seen earlier' scope does not cover the randomness-reuse cases that actually publish M (sub-case 3: M reuse across groups)
unfixed_prior.why_not_fixed: Sub-cases (1) within-record and (2) same-index cross-group are fixed by E2, the KDF(c0_i) clause and the bunker-wide c0 set. Sub-case (3) is not: the adopted hedge r_i = H(... M || A_i || u32be(i) || X) makes the backup/authority c0 repeat across two groups only when that key sits at the same sorted index in both wrap sets; otherwise a stuck RNG produces the same M in two groups with all-fresh c0 values and two different (salted) commits, and no keyless rule fires while every reader of group 1 can derive group 2's DEK. The bunker-wide seen-commit set that D10/R5 cite as the cross-group defence cannot fire at all: dek_commit is salted with group_uid, so two groups never share a commit.
unfixed_prior.fix: See finding 'Hedged r_i indexes by sorted position, so cross-group M reuse under a stuck RNG is detected only by coincidence' below: drop u32be(i) from the hedge (A_i is already unique per E2), optionally hedge m with group_uid || prev, and either drop the bunker-wide commit set or make R5's commit clause compare against all seen commits.

unfixed_prior.prior_title: [MAJOR] crypto-B / authz-A: a recovery that replaces authority or backup is refused (S2) and has no key-handover path
unfixed_prior.why_not_fixed: The authority half is fixed (S2 accepts configured or configured-next; two-key serve; read_secret/S5 open with whichever key the head names). The backup half is now refused by a different rule: G4 makes a backup-replacing recovery a rotate, A4 makes its author head.backup, and the new A5 requires that author to be in recipients(rec), whose pinned part is now {new backup, authority}. 6.4's 'Backup replacement (--backup <id>, a rotate too) needs only the meta update' cannot land on any verifier.
unfixed_prior.fix: See finding 'A5 refuses every backup-key replacement recovery' below.

unfixed_prior.prior_title: [minor] crypto-A: R2/R5 need whole-chain state, but the client-side verifier in 6.1 holds only a pin
unfixed_prior.why_not_fixed: R5 was scoped to 'the records it fetched' for a pin-only client, which is a defensible weakening. But the underlying contract 'verify the tail against the local pin' (6.1 step 1, P1/P2 after a drop) is still not executable: the pin (client file and group_pin) holds group_uid, genesis_hash, head_epoch, head_hash only, and GroupEpochs{since: pinned head} / Hello{have_epoch} return records strictly after it, so the first fetched record's A2 (head.acl), R2 (head.dek_gen/dek_commit), R4 (head.wraps), R6 (recipients(head)) and C4 (head.authority/backup/mode) have no input.
unfixed_prior.fix: See finding 'A verifier holding only a pin cannot verify the first record after it' below.

findings.title: A5 refuses every backup-key replacement recovery
findings.detail: Sequence: operator authors `recovery author --backup K_new --rotate` for group g whose head has backup = K_old. G4: a recovery that replaces backup removes a recipient and MUST be a rotate. A4: author == head.backup == K_old (the only key that may sign it). A5: 'rotate, and recovery with a new generation: author in recipients(rec)'. recipients(rec) = readers(rec) union pinned(rec) = readers union {K_new, authority}; K_old is in neither (pinned ids never appear in acl, and S7 refuses registering a key equal to a configured backup, so it cannot be smuggled in as a reader). Every verifier — server, replica, CLI, auditor — rejects the record with 'A5: ...'. The same happens for a recovery that replaces authority and backup together. 6.4's 'Backup replacement (--backup <id>, a rotate too) needs only the meta update' and Q6's ceremony are therefore unreachable, and section 13's recovery tests do not cover backup replacement so nothing would catch it. Note also the security consequence A5 was written to prevent applies here by construction: the retiring backup key is the party that draws M_new.
findings.fix: Restate A5 for recovery: 'recovery with a new generation: head.backup in recipients(rec) unless rec.backup != head.backup'. State in 6.4 that a backup replacement is authored by, and M_new is drawn by, the retiring key, so a replacement performed because the old backup key is suspect must be followed by an ordinary rotate (admin or authority) to move the live generation off the retired key; a routine replacement needs nothing further. Add the server test 'recovery replacing backup with --rotate lands; next Get works; A5 still refuses a rotate whose author is a removed reader'.

findings.section: 5 S9 / S10 vs 6.3 (server-side revocation) / D13 / 1 ('always wins')
findings.title: S9 and S10 as written refuse the authority's own revocation records, breaking 'removing a compromised identity always wins'
findings.detail: 6.3: 'All server-authored records go through the same verifier'. S9: 'at most one accepted non-rotating record per author per group per 30 s' with no exemption for author == authority. Sequence: t=0 a service admin runs RemoveIdentity(bob); the server authors an authority carry on group g (non-rotating) and it lands. t=10 s RemoveIdentity(carol), who is also a reader of g: the authority carry on g is the second non-rotating record by the same author on the same group inside 30 s -> 'S9: rate'. Either RemoveIdentity fails (6.3 says it is 'never blocked') or the identity row is deleted while carol stays in g's head ACL with a valid wrap, which is the state 6.3's revoked_identity list only tolerates as a lost S2 race. The same applies to two legacy Grant shrinks on one group within 30 s (a TUI service admin kicking two readers). S10 has the same shape: 'while frozen the server answers every non-recovery SubmitEpoch ... with Failed' — if server-authored records go through the verifier, an emergency RemoveIdentity on a frozen group authors nothing, and the pending authority rotate (second half of an earlier revocation) is refused until a recovery lands, so the group stays write-fenced with the kicked key's wrap opening live M. Both rules were added to bound an online rogue admin; the authority is exactly the party they must not bound.
findings.fix: S9: 'per non-authority author'; S10: 'every non-recovery SubmitEpoch from the wire'; add one sentence to 6.3: 'S9 and S10 do not apply to authority-authored carry/rotate or to recovery'. Add the server test: two RemoveIdentity calls within 30 s on identities sharing a group both author a carry; RemoveIdentity on a frozen group still authors its carry and the follow-up rotate lands.

findings.section: 3.3 (hedged r_i) / D10 / 5 R5 (bunker-wide sets) / 3.8 'Confidentiality of M'
findings.title: Hedged r_i indexes by sorted position, so cross-group M reuse under a stuck RNG is detected only by coincidence, and the bunker-wide seen-commit set is inert
findings.detail: 3.3 claims that with a stuck RNG the hedge makes reuse 'reproduce the previous c0 values — which rule R5 refuses — instead of leaking anything', and R5 keeps the c0 and commit sets bunker-wide for that reason. Sequence, one admin client whose OsRng returns a constant X: rotate g1 -> m = reduce(X), M = mB, r_i = H(prefix || M || A_i || u32be(i) || X). Rotate g2 (same admin, or any group where the same client holds admin) -> same m, same M. R2 passes: dek_commit_2 = KDF(M, uid_2) != dek_commit_1 because PRK is salted with group_uid. R5's c0 clause fires only if some recipient present in both groups (the backup key, and the authority in mode A) sits at the same sorted index i in both wrap sets; with different readers in g1 and g2 the index differs, every r_i differs, every c0 is new bunker-wide, and the record is accepted. Result: every reader of g1 holds M and computes DEK_2 = KDF(M, uid_2), with no keyless rule able to notice — the exact cross-group leak (prior finding sub-case 3) the bunker-wide set was introduced to refuse. Second consequence: because commits are group-salted, two groups can never share a dek_commit, so the 'bunker-wide seen-commit set' of R5 is a per-group set in disguise and the text that justifies it is wrong. Third, narrower gap in the same clause: R5 compares KDF(c0_i) only with the record's own dek_commit, so a c0_i equal to an earlier generation's M (r_i = m_old) passes; that publishes M_old, which still opens any pre-rotation snapshot of the database (3.8 says retired pages are scrubbed only best-effort).
findings.fix: Drop u32be(i) from the r_i hedge: r_i = H('secret-bunker-iroh/r/1' || 0x00 || M.compress() || A_i || OsRng 64). A_i is unique within a record (E2) so pairwise distinctness is unchanged, and identical (M, A_i, X) now reproduces an identical c0 wherever the recipient sorts, so the always-present backup (and authority) wrap makes the bunker-wide c0 set refuse a cross-group M reuse deterministically. Optionally hedge m as well (m = from_bytes_mod_order_wide(SHA-512('secret-bunker-iroh/m/1' || 0x00 || group_uid || prev || OsRng 64))) so a stuck RNG cannot repeat M across groups or positions in the first place; R2/R5 then stay as backstops. Extend R5's commit clause to 'KDF(c0_i, group_uid).dek_commit is not in the seen-commit set (which includes this record's)' — n HKDF-Expands and n lookups. Reword D10/R5: the bunker-wide scope matters for c0 only; state the commit set as per group, or keep it bunker-wide with the honest note that it is equivalent. Add the unit test: two groups rotated with the same fixed RandomSource bytes -> second rotate refused by R5.

findings.section: 5 S5 (trial decryption) vs S4 (source matching) / 6.1 server step 2 / 13
findings.title: S5 must skip staged rows whose source no longer matches; otherwise delete+recreate between export and snapshot stalls every client rotation
findings.detail: S4 (under the lock) says a staged row 'whose source no longer matches (deleted and re-created during the window)' is not installed and the live row is a straggler. S5 (outside the lock, against the snapshot) says the server 'decrypts every staged row under the new DEK and AAD, decrypts the row it replaces under the old DEK, and refuses unless the plaintexts are byte-identical'. Sequence: admin exports (name, v1) = 'old' with src (g, n_old); writer runs Delete{name} then Put{name} = 'new' (Put/Delete are not fenced for client rotations); the admin stages the re-encryption of 'old' with src (g, n_old) and submits; the server snapshots (name, v1) = ciphertext of 'new' with nonce n_new; S5 decrypts 'the row it replaces' -> 'new' != 'old' -> Failed{'S5: changed plaintext'}; the client restarts at step 2 (full re-export) and a writer that repeats delete+recreate stalls the rotation indefinitely. The intended behaviour (S4's not-installed + straggler) is unreachable because S5 refuses first. The same ambiguity exists for a staged row whose version no longer exists at snapshot time.
findings.fix: In S5 add: 'a staged row whose (name, version) is absent from the snapshot, or whose (src_dek_gen, src_nonce) differs from the snapshot row's, is excluded from the plaintext check (S4 will not install it; the live row is a straggler)'; the check refuses only when a staged row names a source that exists and decrypts to a different plaintext. Make the 13 test 'delete-then-recreate during the window installs nothing stale' also assert that the submit succeeds and the re-created row is re-encrypted as a straggler.

findings.title: A server-authored rotate that meets an undecryptable retained row never lands, leaving the group write-fenced with the kicked key's wrap opening live M
findings.detail: 6.3: the authority rotate after a revocation is 'retried with backoff until it lands'. S5 applies to server-authored records ('the same verifier') and lists 'undecryptable row' as a rejection; D6 requires every retained version to be re-encrypted. A retained secret_version whose ciphertext or nonce is corrupt, or whose AAD no longer matches (any row that read_secret would already fail on), therefore makes the server's own S5 refuse its own rotate on every retry: needs_rotation stays set, Put answers Failed{'needs-rotation'} forever, and the removed reader's wrap in the pre-carry record keeps opening the live generation — the window D13 promised would be 'seconds'. Today's revoke_read_and_rotate/remove_identity_with_rotations (src/store.rs:734-800) never touch ciphertext and cannot fail this way. Migration step 2 ('decrypt every retained secret_version') has the same unstated failure on a corrupt row.
findings.fix: Specify the policy: a server-authored rotate re-encrypts every row it can open and quarantines the rest (sets a `secret_version.unreadable = 1` flag or deletes the row, audited `rotate-quarantine` with (name, version)), so D6's 'one live generation' holds for readable data and the rotate always lands; GroupStatus/epoch log report quarantined rows. For client rotations keep S5 strict (the client saw the row via ExportGroup, so an undecryptable row there is the client's or the server's bug and should surface). Migration: refuse with the list of unreadable rows unless `--quarantine-unreadable` is given.

findings.section: 6.1 step 1 / 10 P1-P2 and Hello{have} / 11 (client pin file) / 8 (group_pin, group_epoch cascade)
findings.title: A verifier holding only a pin cannot verify the first record after it: A2/R2/R4/R6/C4 need the head record, and the pin stores only hashes
findings.detail: group_pin and the client pin file hold {group_uid, genesis_hash, head_epoch, head_hash}. GroupEpochs{since} returns 'records with epoch > since' and Hello{have_epoch} makes the server ship records after have_epoch. Replica sequence: replica r is a reader of g at epoch 11; an admin kicks r at epoch 12 -> P3 drops the mirror (drop_group_local deletes the secret_group row, src/store.rs; the spec's group_epoch cascades from secret_group, so every record is gone) and keeps the pin at (12, h12). Later r is re-added at epoch 14 by a rewrap, but epoch 13 was an admin carry (w-bit edit). r sends Hello{have: [{g, 12, h12}]}, receives records 13 and 14. To verify 13 it needs: R4 'byte-identical to an entry of head.wraps' (record 12's wraps), A2 'author holds admin in head.acl' (record 12's ACL), R2 head.dek_gen/dek_commit, R6 recipients(head), C4 head.authority/backup/mode. It holds h12 only. The same holds for the CLI at 6.1 step 1 ('GroupEpochs{group, since: pinned head} -> verify the tail against the local pin') and for `client epoch log` on a pin-only client. The verification contract is therefore unspecified precisely where the pin is supposed to be the anchor after a drop or a restart.
findings.fix: State the rule once, in 5 (C2) and 10: a verifier that holds a pin but not the pinned record requests from pin.head_epoch - 1 (GroupEpochs{since: head_epoch - 1}; Hello{have_epoch: head_epoch - 1}), checks that the first returned record's hash equals pin.head_hash, and only then treats it as the head for the rules above. Alternatively store the pinned head's record bytes in group_pin and the client pin file (8-9 KB per group) so the pin is self-sufficient. Add the e2e case: replica revoked at N, re-granted at N+2 with a carry at N+1 in between, converges without a pin reset.
